substantive_units.result: Found and directly replayed an actual n=33,m=142 D2C graph where one star uniquely bridges two vertex-disjoint missing parity pairs. This falsifies the proposed matching-one lemma; the first H_x is K2,2 and cyclic.

Constructed an actual n=39,m=176 D2C graph with H_x equal to two disjoint tree edges, falsifying both the one-tree-component target and h+L<=s. Repaired the exact accounting to h+L<=s+g, where g=(M-I)-nu; the graph satisfies 17<=19 and still has block 30<=rq+s=32.

Extended the actual split-tree obstruction to an exact finite ladder with d=2,...,6 disjoint H_x tree components at joint multiplicity k=2d. This rules out any constant component bound; no infinite family is claimed.

Derived a budgeted density theorem: if the parity/star block exceeds rq+s by epsilon, the full four-centre graph still satisfies m<=M(n) whenever epsilon<=D(u,s). Uniformly D>=9, so exact cancellation was unnecessarily strong.

Combined the unconditional missing-pair ledger with the budget gate: the four-centre branch closes whenever M-I<=D(u,s), in particular whenever s>=ceil((r+q)/2). Any counterexample must have s<(r+q)/2 and M-I>D.

Sharpened the surviving parameter wedge: any four-centre counterexample must have s<ceil((r+q)/2), U>=D+1, rq>=D+1, and both parity populations strictly exceed s/2; equivalently min(r,q)(r+q-min(r,q))>=D+1.

Closed the entire triangle-free parity/star-block subcase by combining Mantel with the five-coordinate complementary-pair cap and a two-case algebraic comparison. Every surviving four-centre counterexample must contain a triangle in that block; the triangle need not use a star because same-parity edges are allowed.

Classified all parity/star-block triangle part patterns. SSS and TSS are impossible; RRS and TTS each force one occupied plus two unoccupied missing parity pairs, while RSS forces two unoccupied pairs.

Closed the apparent one-toll RTS exception: its R-S certificate creates a second T-neighbour of the star, forcing the original T-S edge into the second-kind bucket and a distinct crossed missing pair. Every star-containing block triangle therefore consumes at least two unoccupied missing pairs.

Proved the RTS expansion is locally saturated: the two crossed missing pairs certify all four parity-star arms in pairs, so raw arm criticality cannot force a third missing pair. Any stronger loss must use the present cross edge, fourth cross pair, centre spokes, or coordinate competition.
